rfi.title: Ukraine's allies gather in Paris as Kremlin dismisses 'coalition of warmongers'

Schreckschusswaffe: Kinder nach Klingelstreich mit Waffe verfolgt? Ermittlungen

Irankrieg: US-Militär greift erneut Ziele im Iran an
zeit.description: Die US-Streitkräfte haben weitere Stellungen an der Straße von Hormus angegriffen. Der Iran meldet den Tod von 30 Zivilisten durch US-Luftangriffe. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Start-up Planeteers: Ab ins Meer damit?
zeit.description: Ein Klima-Start-up will CO₂ aus dem Hamburger Hafen in der Nordsee speichern – und die Stadt will mitmachen.

zeit.title: Bürokratieabbau: Bundeskabinett beschließt weitere Schritte zum Bürokratieabbau
zeit.description: Das sogenannte Entlastungskabinett hat bei seiner zweiten Sitzung den Abbau weiterer Vorschriften beschlossen. Jährlich sollen so 600 Millionen Euro eingespart werden.

zeit.title: Ukrainekarte aktuell: Russische Truppen besetzen Dorf bei Sumy
zeit.description: Russische Truppen sind südöstlich der Stadt Sumy vorgedrungen und haben dabei ein Dorf eingenommen. Auch in der Region Donezk kam es zu russischen Vorstößen.

observador.title: Montenegro puxa por Feijóo e critica Costa na imigração
observador.description: Primeiro-ministro ligou-se a Madrid e puxou pela vitória de Feijóo em 2027. Vendeu o milagre económico português aos parceiros do PPE. E atacou falta de "planeamento" dos governos Costa na imigração.

observador.title: Homem detido por maus tratos que levaram à morte de bebé
observador.description: Factos remontam a janeiro, quando a criança de três meses morreu no Hospital de Santa Maria. Após investigação da PJ, o suspeito foi detido e será presente a primeiro interrogatório judicial.

observador.title: Governo promete defender refinaria de Sines
observador.description: "Tudo faremos" para defender interesse estratégico da refinaria de Sines, diz Miranda Sarmento, mas não avança o que será feito.

observador.title: Guerra no Irão recomeçou? — Debate
observador.description: Mísseis, tiros e drones foram lançados e voltaram a intensificar o conflito no Golfo Pérsico. Será esta uma guerra a sério ou uma guerra de faz de conta?

observador.title: Euribor sobe a 3 e a 6 meses para novos máximos desde 2024
observador.description: A Euribor subiu para novos máximos desde março de 2025 e dezembro de 2024. A taxa a três meses, que avançou para 2,490%, continuou abaixo das taxas a seis (2,717%) e a 12 meses (2,916%).

observador.title: Relatório alerta para aumento da extrema-direita em Portugal
observador.description: Relatório considera o "espaço público português" aberto, mas alerta para narrativas xenófobas que aumentam crimes de ódio. Ameaças à liberdade de associação e pressão imobiliária preocupam.

observador.title: ONU lamenta incêndios e pede transição para renováveis
observador.description: Representante da ONU para as alterações climáticas considera que incêndios fazem parte de uma "tendência global de desastres". Diz que país necessita de acelerar transição energética.

observador.title: As notícias das 12h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Benjamin Netanyahu poderá deslocar-se aos EUA este sábado
observador.description: A Reuters avança que Benjamin Netanyahu poderá deslocar-se até aos EUA este sábado. Esta madrugada as forças norte-americanas bombardearam o Irão: morreram 30 pessoas e mais de 260 ficaram feridas.

observador.title: Ministro da Educação: 99% das provas estão classificadas
observador.description: O maior problema prendeu-se com o exame de Português, mas Fernando Alexandre garante que na sexta-feira serão publicadas "todas as avaliações com rigor e com transparência".

observador.title: Reparações. Caraíbas exigem cedência de território a Londres
observador.description: Delegação de países da Comunidade das Caraíbas reuniu-se em Londres para exigir transferência de soberania dos territórios pertencentes à Coroa Britânica. Proposta amplia plano de reparações de 2014.

observador.title: Afinal, não pareceu tão má a eliminação pelos espanhóis
observador.description: Au revoir! A favorita França diz adeus ao Mundial 2026 e falha o que podia ter sido a terceira final consecutiva. Espanha ganhou por 2-0 e chega à segunda final da sua história. Há 16 anos foi campeã.

observador.title: Portuguese girlie Caetana Botelho Afonso terá documentário
observador.description: Depois de Maria Cerqueira Gomes e as irmãs Patrocínio, a Prime Video aposta na jovem influencer portuguesa de 23 anos. O documentário sobre a vida de Caetana Botelho Afonso estreia a 27 de julho.

observador.title: Domínio do português entre exigências para lei TVDE
observador.description: "Lei Uber" com várias alterações controversas. Discutida durante meses, com propostas maioritariamente da direita, segue para redação final e posteriormente, promulgação pelo PR.

observador.title: Ronaldo e Taylor Swift pagaram visto de mãe de Vozinha?
observador.description: Publicações virais no Facebook atribuem o feito a três celebridades mundiais. Mas nenhum órgão de comunicação social nem os próprios o confirmaram. É falso.

observador.title: Irão. EUA restabelecem bloqueio a portos iranianos
observador.description: Nova vaga de ataques norte-americanos a várias áreas no Irão antecedeu o bloqueio do estreito, restabelecido durante a madrugada. EUA têm pelo menos 19 navios de guerra no mar Arábico.

observador.title: Vídeo mostra viagem entre Amesterdão e Paris?
observador.description: Vídeo a circular no Facebook desde final de junho é partilhado por utilizadores com a indicação de que foi filmado num percurso ferroviário entre as capitais dos Países Baixos e França. É verdade?

observador.title: Missão Escola Pública: correção não ficará concluída hoje
observador.description: "Não, não existe resistência. Existe exigência", afirmou a Missão Escola Pública, face às afirmações de Montenegro. Cristina Mota admitiu que classificações não deverão ser afixados na sexta-feira.

france24fr.title: Incendies à Fontainebleau : une forêt marquée par le passage des flammes
france24fr.description: Des incendies ont ravagé environ 2 050 hectares de la célèbre forêt de Fontainebleau, au sud-est de Paris, depuis qu'ils se sont déclarés dimanche 12 juillet. Les feux ont contraint environ 1 000 personnes à évacuer. Quelque 800 pompiers étaient encore à pied d'œuvre mercredi matin pour contenir les reprises de feu, qui ont été fixés la veille après 48 heures de lutte intense. Les explications de Julie Dungelhoeff, notre envoyée spéciale à Achères-la-Forêt

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Argentine sait souffrir et gagner ses matches dans le dernier quart d'heure
france24fr.description: Avec neuf buts marqués après la 80e minute, l’Argentine se montre comme une spécialiste des qualifications au bout de l’effort. Elle a appris à souffrir au fil de la compétition et comptera une nouvelle fois sur le génie de Messi ou l'inspiration tardive de ses attaquants pour battre l'Angleterre en demi-finale du Mondial, mercredi.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ukraine : Ursula von der Leyen annonce un accord entre l'UE et Kiev sur la production de drones
États-Unis : suspension des contrôles routiers de l'ICE après deux décès
france24fr.description: L’administration Trump a ordonné la suspension de la plupart des contrôles routiers menés par l'ICE, alors que deux hommes ont été abattus par des agents en moins d’une semaine.

france24fr.title: Forêt de Fontainebleau : les pompiers cherchent à contenir les reprises de feu, nouvelle garde à vue
france24fr.description: Un homme de 46 ans suspecté d'avoir voulu provoquer un incendie a été interpellé mardi soir sur un parking près de la forêt de Fontainebleau et placé en garde à vue selon une source policière. Mercredi matin, quelque 800 pompiers tentaient toujours de contenir les reprises de feu dans le massif.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Moyen-Orient en direct : l'armée américaine annonce une nouvelle "vague de frappes" en Iran
Mondial 2026 : l'autopsie tactique de la défaite des Bleus en demi-finale
france24fr.description: L'élimination de la France mardi en demi-finales du Mondial face à l'Espagne laisse un goût d'inachevé après les promesses suscitées par le jeu flamboyant déployé tout au long de la compétition. Pour certains, les remplacements de Didier Deschamps durant la rencontre ont considérablement pesé sur cette défaite.

france24fr.title: Mali-Algérie : les deux pays amorcent un rapprochement après une longue crise
france24fr.description: Après plus d’un an de tensions, Bamako et Alger amorcent un retour au dialogue. Les deux pays ont annoncé vendredi la réouverture de leurs espaces aériens respectifs et le retour de leurs ambassadeurs, marquant une première étape vers la normalisation de leurs relations. les précisions de Mohamed Amara, sociologue.

france24fr.title: Chassés d’Afrique du Sud, des Zimbabwéens racontent leur calvaire
france24fr.description: Après des semaines de calvaire, près de 80 000 Zimbabwéens ont regagné leur pays depuis la fin du mois… avec, pour beaucoup, des traumatismes liés aux violences xénophobes en Afrique du Sud. Ils racontent les épreuves qu’ils ont traversées.

france24fr.title: Un squelette de T-Rex vendu 50 millions de dollars à New York, le plus cher jamais vendu
france24fr.description: Un squelette de T-Rex surnommé "Gus" a été vendu mardi pour 50,1 millions de dollars lors d'une vente aux enchères organisée par Sotheby's à New York, devenant le fossile de dinosaure le plus cher jamais vendu.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : reprise des négociations entre le Liban et Israël
france24fr.description: Le Liban et ⁠Israël ont repris mardi ​des discussions dans la capitale italienne, Beyrouth espérant des progrès vers un retrait israélien du sud du Liban dans le cadre d'un accord négocié par les Etats-Unis, malgré des attentes ​limitées quant à des avancées rapides.

france24fr.title: Iran : les Gardiens de la révolution menacent de bloquer d'autres voies d'exportation
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens ont déclaré, mercredi, que ⁠le détroit d'Ormuz resterait fermé jusqu'à la "fin des agressions" américaines. Ils ont par ailleurs menacé de bloquer d'autres "couloirs d'exportation qui bénéficient aux États-Unis et leurs alliés", alors que le blocus ​américain a été rétabli et s'applique aux ports iraniens et aux zones côtières du pays.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RD Congo : l'ampleur de l'épidémie pourrait être 4 fois plus grande, selon l'OMS
france24fr.description: L'ampleur de l'épidémie d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo pourrait dépasser "de deux à quatre fois" les estimations officielles, a indiqué mardi l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS).

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : les États-Unis rétablissent le blocus des ports iraniens
france24fr.description: Les Etats-Unis ont rétabli mardi le blocus ⁠des ports iraniens, ​alors que le président américain Donald Trump est revenu sur son projet, annoncé la veille, de prélever 20% du montant de tout fret transitant par le détroit d'Ormuz.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la ville natale de Jude Bellingham célèbre son héros anglais
france24fr.description: Dans la ville natale de Jude Bellingham, dans les West Midlands au Royaume-Uni, de nombreuses personnes posent devant une fresque murale représentant le milieu de terrain anglais qui a mené les "Three Lions" en demi-finale de la Coupe du monde. france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le rêve des Bleus vire au rouge
france24fr.description: L'élimination de la France en demi-finales du Mondial laisse un goût d'inachevé après les promesses suscitées par le jeu flamboyant déployé tout au long du tournoi, avec comme porte-étendard l'attaque de feu emmenée par Kylian Mbappé, mais après avoir fait tant rêver, Didier Deschamps pourra tout de même quitter les Bleus la tête haute.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: l'Espagne enterre les rêves français en demi-finale
france24fr.description: La France et son attaque jusqu'alors étincelante ont échoué, mardi à Dallas, dans leur quête d'une troisième finale de Coupe du monde consécutive, les hommes de Didier Deschamps ayant été totalement muselés par une équipe d'Espagne parfaitement organisée.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Die Messi-Verschwörung vor dem Halbfinale gegen England
spiegel.description: Die ausgebliebene Rote Karte. Strittige Schiedsrichterentscheidungen. Ungeahndete Fouls. Viele Fans (und auch einige Trainer) stellen sich die Frage, ob Lionel Messi und Argentinien bei der WM bevorzugt werden.

spiegel.title: Griechenland: So rüstet Athen sich gegen die extreme Hitze
spiegel.description: Der Athener Bürgermeister Haris Doukas ist Klimaexperte. Wie er die heißeste Hauptstadt Europas für die Zukunft rüsten will und welche Fehler anderer Metropolen er zu vermeiden versucht.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Schwere Unwetter sorgen für Verletzte und heftige Schäden in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Und wieder Gewitter, Hagel, Starkregen: In Bayern, Baden-Württemberg und Thüringen gab es schwere Schäden durch Unwetter, mehrere Menschen wurden verletzt. Die Gefahr ist noch nicht überall gebannt.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Industrie verliert 177.000 Arbeitsplätze in einem Jahr
spiegel.description: Die schwache Konjunktur belastet den Arbeitsmarkt schwer. Insbesondere die deutsche Industrie trifft es hart. 2025 gingen im verarbeitenden Gewerbe 177.000 Arbeitsplätze verloren.

spiegel.title: AfD-Verbot in Thüringen? Hape Kerkeling soll bei Anhörung sprechen
spiegel.description: Sollten einzelne AfD-Landesverbände verboten werden? Darüber gab es in der Politik zuletzt eine Debatte, nun soll diese Frage auch im Landtag in Erfurt erörtert werden. Auf der Rednerliste: Entertainer Hape Kerkeling.

spiegel.title: Phil Collins: Noel Gallagher hält mich nicht wirklich für den Antichristen
spiegel.description: Oasis-Songwriter Noel Gallagher hat häufig über Genesis-Frontmann Phil Collins gelästert. Nun könnten sich die beiden bei einer Preisverleihung begegnen. Collins glaubt zu wissen, welcher Song Gallagher getriggert hat.

spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Das sagt der CDU-Kanzler auf seiner Sommerpressekonferenz
spiegel.description: In Berlin tritt Friedrich Merz vor die Hauptstadtpresse. Die Bezeichnung als »Außenkanzler« stört ihn nicht, sagt der Kanzler, beim Thema Unterhaltszuschuss verteidigt er die geplante Kürzung. Die Pressekonferenz im Video und der Liveanalyse.

spiegel.title: Kita-Rechtsanspruch: Studie zeigt mehr Elternzeit bei Vätern und schnellere Rückkehr von Müttern
spiegel.description: Seit 13 Jahren haben Eltern Anspruch auf einen Kitaplatz für ihr Kind ab dessen erstem Geburtstag. Eine Studie zeigt: Das verändert, wer zu Hause bleibt – und wer arbeiten geht.

spiegel.title: Kylie Jenner: Aktivisten entstellen Werbung für Metas KI-Brillen
spiegel.description: Kylie Jenner wirbt für KI-Brillen von Mark Zuckerbergs Konzern Meta. Doch die Kritik nimmt zu, in London wurde ein Plakat nun öffentlichkeitswirksam umgestaltet.

spiegel.title: Gelendschik: Ukrainische Seedrohne zerstört offenbar russisches FSB-Schiff in Schwarzmeerhafen
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine hat nach eigenen Angaben ein Patrouillenschiff des russischen Geheimdiensts FSB schwer getroffen. Für Kyjiw ist der Schlag weit hinter den eigenen Linien offenbar von doppelter symbolischer Bedeutung.

spiegel.title: John Lennon warnte Mick Jagger vor Elvis Presley
spiegel.description: Auf einer Tour der Beatles traf John Lennon einst sein Idol Elvis Presley. Offenbar eine so ernüchternde Erfahrung, dass er seinen Kollegen von den Rolling Stones von einem Treffen abriet.

spiegel.title: Schulden: Erkrankungen und Jobverlust sind häufigste Gründe für Überschuldung in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Menschen in Deutschland geraten vor allem wegen Erkrankungen, Sucht oder Unfällen in Finanznot. Laut Daten von Beratungsstellen unterscheidet sich die durchschnittliche Höhe der Schulden bei Männern und Frauen erheblich.

spiegel.title: Historische Bürgerwehr in Bayern: Warum sich Bürger einst für die Demokratie bewaffneten
spiegel.description: Viele denken bei Bürgerwehren an Selbstjustiz. Dabei haben sie einen ganz anderen Ursprung: 1848 wollten Demokraten damit ihr Gemeinwesen verteidigen. Im bayerischen Königsberg sind sie der Idee bis heute treu.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: CDU mobilisiert bundesweit Mitglieder für den Wahlkampf gegen die AfD
spiegel.description: Im CDU-Bulli quer durchs Land: Die Parteispitze appelliert an alle Mitglieder, beim Wahlkampf gegen die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt mit anzupacken. Generalsekretär Linnemann verspricht »einmalige Erlebnisse und Erfahrungen«.

spiegel.title: Diesel wird im Wochenvergleich um fast zwölf Cent teurer
spiegel.description: Diesel und Benzin haben sich kräftig verteuert. Preistreiber dürften die erneut stärkeren Spannungen zwischen Iran und USA sein.

spiegel.title: Meghan Markle: Herzogin für Netflix-Show »With Love, Meghan« für Daytime Emmy nominiert
spiegel.description: TV-Kritiker verspotteten die Kochsendung »With Love, Meghan«. Jetzt hat die Ehefrau von Prinz Harry trotzdem Chancen auf einen Fernsehpreis – der allerdings nicht ganz so prestigeträchtig ist, wie man meinen könnte.

spiegel.title: Dua Lipa stellt sich gegen Albanien-Pläne des Trump-Clans
spiegel.description: Ein geplantes Luxusresort von Trump-Schwiegersohn Jared Kushner in einem Naturschutzgebiet treibt die Albaner auf die Straße. Die Musikerin Dua Lipa, deren Eltern aus Kosovo und Albanien stammen, hat nun verraten, was sie von dem Projekt hält.

phys-org.description: In the aftermath of the devastating July 4, 2025, floods that took 139 lives in Central Texas, an associate professor at The University of Texas at Austin set out to make a new type of outdoor flood alarm: a low-tech, loud alarm that anyone could "set and forget"—just like a smoke detector.

phys-org.title: Q&A: What does the 2026 World Cup reveal about modern sport?
phys-org.description: It's the final week of the 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup. Over the last month, there have been plenty of highs and lows both on and off the pitch, from the overnight popularity of Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha and the Norwegian row to the questionable use of Video Assistant Referee (VAR) and inconsistent enforcement of fouls by referees, leading concerns about match fixing.

phys-org.title: Biodiversity boosts productivity most during extreme drought in drier grasslands
phys-org.description: When extreme drought strikes, drier grasslands receive the greatest productivity benefit from biodiversity. By contrast, forests did not show the same context-dependent pattern under drought, according to a new global synthesis of 75 biodiversity experiments. Researchers from Yokohama National University published their results in Nature Ecology & Evolution on July 15.

phys-org.title: Generative AI's power sparks fears of dumbing humans down
phys-org.description: Generative AI chatbots capable of writing emails and computer code, translating, organizing a trip or coming up with gift ideas are now readily available, prompting some to ask whether human brainpower could suffer for lack of use.

phys-org.title: The secret to hydrogen's quantum behavior lies in symmetry
phys-org.description: As interest in clean hydrogen power grows, so does the need for safe storage and transportation materials. One such material, vanadium, is a leading candidate because it readily absorbs hydrogen and allows it to move through its crystal structure. However, hydrogen displays varying behavior in the presence of vanadium, with the underlying cause remaining unclear.

phys-org.title: Wildfires expose millions in the Midwest and Northeast US to dangerous smoke
phys-org.description: Heavy smoke from several large wildfires blazing in Canada and Minnesota is expected to engulf large swaths of the Midwest and Northeast U.S. this week, exposing millions of people to dangerous air pollution.

phys-org.title: Face-to-face with ancient Rome: Exhibition in Hungary brings forgotten faces to life
phys-org.description: A blacksmith, a stable boy, a soldier, a slave: The faces and stories of these and other residents of an ancient Roman city in modern Hungary have been brought to life in remarkable fidelity for a new exhibition in Budapest.

phys-org.title: Elephants turn footsteps into messages through ground and skull vibrations
phys-org.description: Elephants can communicate with other elephants across distances of up to five kilometers (3 miles) by producing sounds that travel through the air. However, they have a second way of sending signals: seismic waves traveling through the ground. These vibrations are transmitted from elephants' feet through their legs and ultimately through the bones of their skull directly into the inner ear. phys-org.title: AI explored as tool for unraveling radicalization's complex drivers
phys-org.description: Radicalization is a complex process, influenced by many variables that interact to varying degrees. AI scientist Mijke van den Hurk investigated whether artificial intelligence could help unravel this intricate interplay. She defended her Ph.D. thesis cum laude on June 29.

phys-org.title: Nitrate in drinking water may be linked to preterm births in New Zealand
phys-org.description: A new Aotearoa New Zealand study has found that nitrate concentrations in drinking water are associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, even at levels well below the current drinking water standard. The study, published in Environmental Research, analyzed 735,831 singleton births between 2008 and 2021, linking gestational age with estimated nitrate concentrations in drinking water at the mother's usual residence.

phys-org.title: When words signal conflict: Measuring exclusionary nationalism in prewar Japan
phys-org.description: Why do countries go to war? While economic, military and geopolitical factors are often part of the answer, researchers have also pointed to exclusionary nationalism—the belief that one's own nation is superior to others. One observable trace of such sentiment is language: As exclusionary attitudes intensify, people tend to favor words from their own language over foreign ones and even reject the "enemy's" words outright.

phys-org.title: Low carbon dioxide levels improve microbial production of biodegradable plastic
phys-org.description: In an innovative gas fermentation process, reducing the concentration of carbon dioxide was found to significantly improve microbial production of the biodegradable plastic poly[(R)-3-hydroxybutyrate]. Researchers found that hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria grown under safe, nonflammable gas conditions enable more efficient production of biodegradable plastic at lower CO2 levels. The study provides a promising strategy for sustainable carbon recycling and efficient CO2 utilization.

phys-org.title: Report details ecological characterization of peatlands and coastal lagoons in EU
phys-org.description: A new synthesis report, titled "Ecological Characterisation of Peatlands and Coastal Lagoons in Europe," has been published to support the assessment, monitoring and restoration of European wetlands under EU environmental legislation. phys-org.description: The mystery of why some amphibian populations recover following outbreaks of a deadly fungus has been solved in a new study led by University College London (UCL), ZSL and Imperial College London.

phys-org.title: More than 50% of Australian university assignments used AI. How should universities respond?
phys-org.description: Last week, the U.S. software company Turnitin revealed 53.6% of Australian tertiary education submissions run through its system used some form of AI in the period from October 2025–April 2026. undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

proj-syn.title: The West’s Turkey Dilemma
proj-syn.description: Few countries better illustrate the difficult trade-off between democratic principles and strategic necessity than Turkey. As the country’s geopolitical and economic importance grows, NATO allies are becoming increasingly willing to overlook President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s attacks on democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: How the Tech Lords Hacked the Firm
proj-syn.description: A handful of tech oligarchs have figured out how to tap public markets without submitting to shareholder oversight. The recent SpaceX IPO represents the culmination of this process, granting Elon Musk near-total authority and revealing how thoroughly the mechanisms meant to hold corporate leaders accountable have been weakened.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Real Energy Test
proj-syn.description: The Iran war has underscored the fragility of global energy markets, exposing which economies can withstand repeated shocks and which cannot. For ASEAN+3 countries, resilience will depend on stronger electricity systems, regional cooperation, and institutions that can manage persistent uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The US Economy Cannot Grow Without Renewables
proj-syn.description: Consumption demand, which has long powered America’s formidable economy, rests on the promise of cheap energy. But the Trump administration has conflated that with fossil fuels, confusing historic correlation with causation and, in the process, jeopardizing long-term prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Purpose of Development Cooperation Is to Be Unnecessary
proj-syn.description: The original promise of development cooperation was to help countries overcome poverty, build productive economies, and reduce their dependence on external resources. That has not happened, and ongoing reviews of development cooperation, which focus on donor countries' needs and priorities, are unlikely to change this.

proj-syn.title: Oil Shocks Are No Longer So Shocking
proj-syn.description: Despite this year's US/Israeli-Iran war causing the largest-ever disruption to global oil supplies, the shocks of the 1970s had a greater impact. Because oil has been used as a weapon for so long, markets, policymakers, and strategists have adapted.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.
